surprises.description: Public Storage’s Q3 core FFO was $4.34 per share, $0.07 above the preview’s $4.27 consensus. That also exceeded the preview’s base-case range of $4.26–$4.31 only slightly, while landing within its bull-case range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Core FFO / share | Consensus | $4.27”; the preview’s bull scenario was “$4.33–4.38.”

surprises.description: The company raised full-year core FFO guidance by $0.10 and set a $17.00 midpoint, modestly above the preview’s base-case midpoint expectation of about $16.93. The new range also extends above the preview’s bull-case high end of $17.05.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 core FFO guidance for the second time this year, increasing it by $0.10 (0.6%) to a range of $16.90-$17.10 with a midpoint of $17.00.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected guidance “narrowed to $16.85–$17.00 (mid ~$16.93)”; the bull case expected “$16.95–$17.05.”

surprises.description: Move-in rents accelerated far more than the preview’s expectation of continued strength: they rose 9.3% year over year, versus a Q2 baseline of 1.6% and June’s 4% pace. Management expects that sharp increase to moderate in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average move-in rents rose 9% year-over-year (9.3%) in Q3—the strongest level since Q2 2022 and up 28% from Q4 2025—though management expects this to moderate in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q2 move-in rent growth of “+1.6%,” June at “+4%,” and said management guided to “continued strength.”

surprises.description: Same-store revenue returned to positive growth at 0.5%, beating the preview’s expectation of roughly flat to modestly negative Q3 growth. The 110-basis-point sequential acceleration made the recovery more pronounced than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-store revenue and NOI each grew just 0.5% in Q3, but same-store revenue accelerated 110 basis points sequentially from Q2 into positive territory.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q3 revenue should be “at or better than roughly −0.4%” and gave a base-case range of “−0.4% to 0.0%.”

surprises.description: Full-year same-store guidance improved to +0.25% revenue growth and -0.3% NOI growth. Those outcomes are at or near the favorable ends of the ranges shown in the preview, with the company citing meaningful help from Los Angeles.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year same-store revenue and NOI guidance was raised to +0.25% and -0.3% respectively, improvements of 45 and 85 basis points, with roughly half the revenue lift coming from the Los Angeles recovery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed existing FY2026 guidance of “Same-store revenue growth” from “(0.7)%” to “0.3%” and “Same-store NOI growth” from “(2.0)%” to “(0.3)%.”

surprises.description: The Los Angeles portfolio returned to positive revenue growth, and management quantified a remaining $35–40 million of recapture upside across 2027 and 2028. The preview expected phased recapture to begin in Q3 and said quantification would be useful, but did not anticipate a return to positive growth already in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Los Angeles portfolio returned to positive revenue growth after state-of-emergency pricing restrictions expired, with roughly 100 basis points of revenue recapture remaining, representing $35-40 million of upside expected across 2027 and 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Q3 as “the first quarter of the ‘measured and phased’ recapture” and said, “Any quantification of recapture pace is a genuine 2027 estimate input.”

surprises.description: NSA showed stronger early operating traction than the preview’s discussion of integration risk and targeted unit reactivation alone suggested: move-in volumes rose more than 30% in August and September, and the company identified over $100 million of ROI opportunities.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The NSA portfolio showed move-in volumes up over 30% in August and September after rebranding,” with “roughly 14,000 inherited vacant/unrentable units being returned to the rental pool and over $100 million of ROI opportunities identified.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “the ~14,000 units targeted for reactivation” and “NSA performance on the PS Next platform,” and noted that execution risk was “largely behind them.”

surprises.description: Net debt-to-EBITDA was 3.4x, above the 2.9x figure cited in the preview. Management attributed 0.4 turns of temporary elevation to transaction timing and said the acquisitions should be slightly deleveraging over time, but leverage was still higher than the stated reference level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The balance sheet remains among the strongest in the REIT sector with net debt-to-EBITDA of 3.4x, though metrics were temporarily elevated 0.4 turns due to transaction timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “leverage (net debt/EBITDA 2.9x; 4.2x incl. preferred).”
